notes: Access: plain direct HTTP fetch, no WAF/bot-block. Discovery: homepage's rendered link list included '/new-1/' (canonical, react-helmet title 'New Products from Sur La Table'). That page itself shows '0 Items' twice in its own rendered HTML - it carries no directly-assigned products and is a pure grouping/hub page - but it links out to 8 real department children at /new/<dept>/, each confirmed a genuine 'New in <Dept>' PLP with its own exact 'N Items' header and matching 'Showing 24 of N' pagination footer. The sitemap also listed /new-in-coffee/ and /new-in-small-appliances/ as separate URLs; both were verified (curl -L) to be 301 redirects to the canonical /new/coffee-tea/ and /new/small-appliances/ respectively - true aliases, not separate listings, so not recorded as their own rows. Checked and EXCLUDED as not New Arrivals: nothing else on the sitemap matched 'new-in'/'new-arriv'/'just-in'/'latest'/'whats-new' beyond the two aliases above; no 'New Collection'/'New Season'/'New Range' style page was found anywhere in the sitemap category list. Site search was not used since robots.txt disallows /search*; sitemap + homepage nav + breadcrumb evidence was sufficient and is the stronger signal anyway. No local-language variants applicable (US English-only site).
